title: The roundup issue is a living Story: automatic fill, human steering, scheduled approval, exactly-once send
description:
**Goal.** The roundup/issue is a living Story that sits on the board all week, receives qualifying items automatically, and lets people steer it: humans edit the copy, a machine fills the slots, and neither overwrites the other. An admin approves it for a time; the site backend sends it exactly once with nobody present; the web archive keeps working. The newsletter plugin's issue, approval, scheduler and send-ledger code is deleted. (Ryan, 2026-11-12: "a semi-automated algorithm that gives people a chance to steer it... a Story that sits there all week, getting updates.")

**Design.**
- **The issue is a Story** (Item of type `newsletter-issue` in the archive section), one per list and period. It is created automatically at the start of the period by the scheduler in the publication time zone (the period key and claim already exist in `newsletter/roundup.py`: `period_key`, `_claim_period`, so a retry never makes two). It stays in Draft and open until it is sent. The cadence comes from the list; nothing is hard-coded.
- **Defined blocks, one owner each.** The Story body is a fixed set of blocks. Machine-owned: the item entries inside each section slot (an entry is a reference to a Reference or Story by id, with `addedBy`, `addedAt` and the reason, and renders the item's own headline and dek). Human-owned: subject, preheader, intro, outro, section headings, an optional per-entry copy override, and entry order pins. The inserter (PPY-849bf1) writes only machine blocks, only by adding or removing machine entries, and never touches a human-owned field.
- **Contribution rules (no overwriting).** The Story is already append-only and versioned: every edit is a new version carrying the actor (person or agent name). On top of that: (1) a write names the blocks it touches and is conditional on the version it started from; (2) if the newest version changed meanwhile, the loser reloads and re-applies only its own block change. Blocks are disjoint by ownership, so this is a rebase, not a text merge; (3) a human edit to a machine entry (its copy override, its position, or marking it keep) PINS that entry: from then on the machine never changes, moves or removes it for ordinary reasons; (4) once a human has touched a human-owned field, only humans change it; an agent that wants to change it posts a suggestion in the Story's Conversation instead of writing the field; (5) an agent may write a human-owned field only while no human has touched it since the agent's base version. Why this and not a lock or a 3-way merge: a lock held by someone who walks away would stall a Story that is open for a week, and a 3-way merge of prose is complexity we do not need once ownership already separates the text. One version log, disjoint blocks, conditional write: the simplest thing that fits the existing Story version model.
- **Exclusions ("removed by a human").** A person removing an entry writes an exclusion record on the Story (append-only, in the version history): the Reference or Story id, the issue, who, when, and why (one short reason, required). The inserter never re-adds an excluded id for that issue. Exclusions are listed in the Story under "Left out" with who, when and why, and a person can restore one (a new record marks it restored; nothing is deleted). An exclusion is per issue: it does not hide the item from other surfaces, and later issues consider the item afresh only if it was not already sent.
- **Below the floor after insertion.** The three-star floor (PPY-0e8d66) outranks pins. If an entry falls below the floor the machine removes it, even a pinned one, and records "removed: below floor" (not a human exclusion). If it is re-rated up, the inserter may add it back with its human copy override intact, unless a person excluded it.
- **Approval and send.** Approval stays admin-only scheduling: an admin approves a version for a time in the publication zone (stored UTC), recording the content hash of the rendered issue. From approval until send the inserter is paused. At fire time Caducus re-checks "still approved and unchanged" by hash. Any edit after approval, by a person or by a below-floor removal, returns the issue to draft ("edited after approval; approve again"), unpauses the inserter, and nothing is sent. The send happens once at the scheduled time through the send ledger keyed (issue, recipient). An issue with no entries cannot be approved; if the period ends with none, no issue is sent and admins are told. The web archive page is published when the issue is sent.
- Caducus gets the generic part (scheduled digest, approval record, schedule, ledger, fan-out, dead letter); Papyrus supplies the Story, the blocks and the panel.

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: The issue is a living Story
  Scenario: Created with the period
    Given a weekly list whose new period begins
    Then one issue Story is created, in draft, open for the whole period
    And a retry of the scheduler creates no second issue for that period

  Scenario: An item arrives mid-week
    Given the issue is open on Wednesday
    When an article reaches three stars
    Then the inserter adds it to its section slot as a machine entry
    And the Story shows the new version with the inserter as the actor and the reason
    And the intro, subject and every human edit are exactly as they were

  Scenario: A duplicate arrives
    Given the issue already holds an article about a story
    When another article of the same story group arrives
    Then it is not added and the Story lists it under Left out as a duplicate of the first

  Scenario: A human removes an item and the inserter runs again
    Given an editor removed an entry with a reason
    When the inserter runs again, including after other items arrive
    Then the entry is not added back
    And the Story shows who removed it, when and why, with a Restore action

  Scenario: A human edits machine copy
    Given a machine entry in the issue
    When an editor rewrites that entry's blurb
    Then the entry is pinned and keeps the editor's words
    And the inserter never changes, moves or removes it for ordinary reasons

  Scenario: An agent and a human edit at the same time
    Given an agent and an editor both started from the same version
    When the agent writes its machine block and the editor writes the intro
    Then both changes are kept, as two versions with two actors
    And when both wrote the same field, the second writer is told, sees the newer text and decides, and nothing is overwritten silently

  Scenario: An agent cannot overwrite a person's words
    Given an editor edited the intro
    When an agent wants to improve it
    Then the agent posts a suggestion in the Story's conversation and the intro is unchanged

  Scenario: An item falls below three stars after insertion
    Given an entry is in the issue
    When its rating is lowered to two stars
    Then the entry is removed with the reason "below floor", even if an editor pinned it
    And if it is rated three stars again it can be added back with the editor's copy

  Scenario: Approval then edit returns to draft
    Given an admin approved the issue for Monday 04:00 in the publication zone
    When an editor changes the intro on Sunday
    Then the issue returns to draft, nothing is scheduled to send, and the inserter resumes

  Scenario: Approved and unchanged sends once
    Given an approved, unchanged issue
    When the time passes and the sender runs twice (retry)
    Then every confirmed subscriber receives it exactly once

  Scenario: Only admins approve
    When an editor tries to approve
    Then it is refused

  Scenario: No approval, no issue
    Given nobody approved the issue
    When the time passes
    Then nothing is sent and admins are told it was missed

  Scenario: Empty issue
    Given an issue with no entries
    Then it cannot be approved, and if the period ends nothing is sent and admins are told

  Scenario: Failure mid-send
    Given the send fails after half the recipients
    When it resumes
    Then the first half is not mailed again and the rest are

  Scenario: Suppressed and paused
    Given a subscriber is suppressed or the site is paused
    Then they are skipped, or nothing goes out, and the issue shows why

  Scenario: Web archive
    When an issue is sent
    Then its archive page is published with the same content
```

**Depends on:** ownership story; PPY-0e8d66 (three-star floor). Blocks the selection story (PPY-849bf1) and MoM launch.
**Related:** PPY-19a098 (M2 as built), PPY-31455f decisions of 2026-10-20 (admins approve, scheduler, hash re-check), PPY-849bf1 (what the inserter adds).

**Open questions for Ryan:** (1) Who may remove an entry or edit copy: any editor (proposed), or only admins? Only admins schedule either way. (2) Must a person give a reason when removing an item? Proposed: yes, one short line. (3) If an item falls below three stars after you approved, return the issue to draft (proposed) or quietly drop that item and still send? (4) When an older article finally gets its third star, does it count as new this week? Proposed: yes, by when it became eligible, not when it was published. (5) Keep the web archive as a page per issue as today, and one approver per site or any admin? Proposed: keep, any admin.
